title: Sort by column from the keyboard and announce the sort state
problem: A header that sorts on click is invisible to anyone who cannot use a mouse, and a sort that only changes the row order gives a screen reader user no way to know what happened or which column is now sorted.
context: Builds on the static native table. Sorting happens in the component over the rows it was given.
impact: Sorting is the first interactive feature. This is where the component either meets its accessibility requirement or starts accumulating exceptions to it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The design names the explicit accessibility requirement being tested against, such as specific WCAG 2.2 success criteria, before implementation begins.
Each sortable header contains a native button control. Activating it with Enter or Space sorts by that column, and activating it again reverses the direction.
The sorted header carries aria-sort with the current direction, and no other header claims a sort.
Sorting is stable, and rows with missing values sort consistently to one documented end in both directions.
Focus stays on the activated control after sorting, and the focus indicator is visible.
Automated tests drive sorting through keyboard events, not by calling internal functions, and cover direction reversal, stability and missing values. All pass at the submitted revision.
The learner records a manual check with at least one screen reader, naming the reader and browser and what was announced.
The learner explains why a button inside the header was chosen over a clickable header cell, and one sort behavior that would still confuse a screen reader user.

constraints: The component itself uses no runtime dependencies. TypeScript, a test runner and a DOM implementation for tests are the only development dependencies.
Sorting is in memory over the supplied rows. Do not introduce a data source or asynchronous loading yet.
Do not push to a remote or open a pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: Sort interaction, its programmatic state and its keyboard behavior.

investigation_areas: What the accessibility requirement actually says about name, role, value and keyboard operation
What aria-sort communicates and where it must and must not appear
Which parts of the behavior a DOM implementation in tests can verify and which only a real browser and screen reader can
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design.
documentation_requirements: Record the accessibility requirement, what is tested automatically, and what was checked by hand.
